transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

I guess mostly my sleep. It’s been really messed up lately—like I’ll be up half the night and my mind just won’t slow down, and then other times I wake up way too early and feel like I didn’t rest at all. I keep trying to just push through it because I’ve got work stuff, bookkeeping and all that, but then I’m just sitting there staring at numbers and thinking about how I didn’t sleep… so, yeah, that’s why I came in.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood lately, like feeling down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah… I mean, I think so. I’ve been waking up with this really heavy, empty feeling, like before anything even happens that day. It’s weird because I’ll be sitting in my condo—you know, the place I worked so hard to get, and I used to feel proud of it—and lately it just makes me want to cry for no clear reason. I keep thinking I should feel grateful, and then I feel worse because I don’t.
Have you been feeling like you’re a failure or that you’ve let people down lately?

Yeah… kind of a lot, actually. I keep telling myself I was stupid to take on the mortgage, like, who did I think I was doing that? And then I start thinking I’ve let everyone down somehow, even though—this is the dumb part—no bill is actually late. It’s not like anything has happened yet. I just sit there looking at the paperwork or even just thinking about it, and it turns into this whole thing in my head.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about different things—like work, relationships, or other responsibilities—beyond just the mortgage or sleep?

I’m not really sure… I mean, I worry, but it’s hard to tell what’s “excessive,” you know? Work stuff gets in my head sometimes, but then I’ll be thinking about one receipt I maybe filed wrong and suddenly I’m remembering this teacher in high school who used to make us redo the whole assignment if the margins were off—which is not really related, sorry.

I guess it kind of all blends together lately, but I don’t know if it’s different things exactly or just the same few things looping around.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms lately, like restlessness, feeling on edge, muscle tension, or being easily fatigued?

Yeah… mostly tired, I guess. Like, even if I technically spend the whole night in bed, getting from the parking lot into the office feels ridiculous, like I’m dragging sandbags or something. And then by lunch my brain feels kind of used up, like I’ve already done a full day.

It’s annoying because my job is mostly numbers and little details, and I used to be able to just… do it. I don’t know, even walking in feels like too much sometimes.
Have you found that things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with friends, no longer feel satisfying or make you feel happy?

Yeah… I think so. I stopped going to salsa class, which is weird because I used to really look forward to it—well, I also hated the parking situation there, but that wasn’t why I stopped. And my paints are still sitting out on the table at home. Like, the brushes and everything are just there, and I look at them and feel… nothing. Almost like they belong to somebody else, not me.
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly than usual, or on the flip side, feeling restless and unable to sit still?

Yeah, kind of both, actually. At work I catch myself moving really slow sometimes, like I’ll just stare at the calculator before I even press the buttons, and then I’m annoyed because it’s just a calculator, you know?

But then other times I’m the opposite, like shuffling receipts around or fidgeting with them and I can’t really sit still. I’ll straighten a stack, then mess it up again, which reminds me of when my aunt used to organize coupons by expiration date—sorry, that’s not the point. It’s just… yeah, slow and restless, depending on the moment.
Have you ever had sudden episodes where you felt intense fear or discomfort that came out of nowhere, like your heart was racing, you couldn’t breathe, or you felt like you were losing control?

I don’t think so? I mean, I get uncomfortable sometimes, but not like… out of nowhere my heart is pounding and I can’t breathe. At least not that I’ve noticed.

Sometimes I’ll feel weird in a crowded store, but then I’m also trying to remember if I bought paper towels, and the lights are terrible in there—sorry, that’s not really what you asked. I guess no, I haven’t had those sudden fear episodes like that.
Have you found it hard to control your worrying, like it keeps going even when you try to focus on something else?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I do worry about normal stuff, like work and whether I entered something wrong, or if I forgot to pay a bill—well, not my bill, like at work, which is different. And then I’ll try to focus on something else and sometimes I can, sometimes I just end up thinking about what I’m supposed to make for dinner or how my fridge makes that clicking noise.

So… I don’t know if I’d say it’s hard to control exactly. I haven’t really paid attention to it that way.
Can you describe what your mood feels like most days—like, is there a constant heaviness or sadness, or does it come and go depending on what’s happening around you?

Most days lately it’s more like I wake up and it’s already there, this heavy, empty feeling. Like before anything even happens, before I check my phone or make coffee or whatever.

And it’s weird because I’ll be sitting in my condo, which I worked really hard to get, and I should feel proud or settled or something… but instead I just feel like I could cry. Like the walls are fine, the place is fine, I picked the little kitchen shelves myself—sorry, that’s not really important. It just feels heavy even when nothing specific is going wrong.
Is there anything you do anymore that truly makes you feel good or brings you a sense of pleasure, even for a little while?

Not really. I mean, I used to go to salsa class, and that was fun even when I was terrible at it—there was this one instructor who always counted too loud, which somehow helped—but I stopped going.

And I still have my paints sitting out on the table at home. They’ve been there long enough that I probably should clean them up, but I just look at them and feel… nothing. Like they belong to somebody else, not me. So I guess things that used to make me feel good don’t really do much anymore.
Do you find that you're moving much slower than usual or, the opposite, feeling so restless that you can't sit still most days?

Yeah… I think both, kind of. At work I’ll catch myself moving really slow, like I’m just staring at the calculator before I even press the buttons. Which is stupid because it’s literally my job, you know, numbers and receipts and all that.

But then other times I’m the opposite. I’ll be fidgeting with the receipts, lining them up or messing with the edges, and I can’t really sit still. We have these little paper clips too, and I’ll keep bending them without realizing it—sorry, that’s probably not the point. So yeah, slower sometimes, restless other times.
Do you feel like you don’t have any energy left, even if you haven’t done anything physically exhausting?

Yeah. It’s like… I can sleep the whole night, or at least be in bed the whole night, and still feel completely wiped out.

Even just walking from the parking lot into the office feels ridiculous, like my legs are dragging sandbags or something. And it’s not even a long walk—there’s this one spot by the little tree where people always park crooked, and I get annoyed about that, but anyway… by the time I’m at my desk I already feel tired.

By lunch, my brain feels worn out too. Like I haven’t done anything that should exhaust me, but I feel used up.
Have you had any thoughts about death or dying, or if it would be better if you weren’t around anymore?

I… I don’t know. I mean, I don’t think so? Not in a clear way like that.

Sometimes I get this thought that people at work would probably have an easier time if I wasn’t slowing things down, but then I start thinking about how last week the printer jammed three times and everyone blamed the toner even though it was the paper tray, and I was the one who fixed it, so… I guess that’s not really what you asked.

Death feels like a big word. I don’t sit there planning anything, if that’s what you mean. I just have moments where I kind of wish everything would stop for a while. Does that count?
Have you had any thoughts about not wanting to wake up in the morning or that it would be easier if you just didn’t have to deal with each day?

I’m not really sure. I don’t wake up thinking, like, “I wish I hadn’t woken up,” exactly.

It’s more like… the morning feels heavy sometimes, and I’ll lie there thinking about everything I have to do, like getting dressed and getting to work and whether I remembered to put the receipts in the right folder—because if I don’t, it turns into this whole mess later. But I don’t know if that’s the same as not wanting to wake up.

I guess I just wish I could skip the day sometimes, maybe. Not disappear, just… not have to do all of it.
